[iOS] Notify when proxy configurations are set on WebKit

web::ProxyConfigurationProvider maps proxy rules to native proxy
configurations on a background thread, then sets them on the
WKWebsiteDataStore. Callers can now register a callback that runs on the
main sequence once the configurations of an UpdateProxyConfiguration()
call are set on the data store. It gets the ID of that call, which
UpdateProxyConfiguration() now returns, and the number of
configurations. A call canceled by a newer one isn't reported.

A follow-up CL uses it to record how long Secure Gateway routing rules
take to be set on WebKit, and how many native configurations WebKit
gets for them.

[Glic] Return GlicInvocationHandle and cancel owned trigger invokes

Return a GlicInvocationHandle from GlicKeyedService::Invoke(),
GlicKeyedService::InvokeWithAutoSubmit(), and
GlicInstanceCoordinator::Invoke() instead of raw
base::WeakPtr<GlicInstance>.

GlicInvocationHandle exposes explicit operator bool(), instance(), and
Cancel(), binding cancellation to GlicInvokeHandler::GetWeakPtr() before
Invoke() runs so cancelling a completed, superseded, or
already-cancelled invocation is a safe no-op without cancelling
unrelated invocations on the same GlicInstance. Implicit construction
from base::WeakPtr<GlicInstance> keeps existing test mocks compiling.

Wire ExperimentalTriggeringUpdatesHandler to store pending
GlicInvocationHandles by invoke id and cancel remaining in-flight
invocations in StopOwnedLiveWork() and handler destruction.

Metrics note: cancelling an in-flight invocation routes through
GlicInvokeHandler::OnError(GlicInvokeError::kCancelled) (CUI outcome
kUnknownCancel). Invocations that previously waited in
WaitForActuationTask until the 5-minute timeout when a session ended
without an actor task will now shift from kTimeout to kCancelled.

media: Skip MediaFoundationPackageLocatorTest.HEVC before Windows 10 RS3

MediaFoundationPackageLocatorTest.HEVC asserts that Store HEVC package
install paths exist whenever CanMfDecodeCodec(HEVC) returns true. Before
Windows 10 RS3, Windows shipped an inbox HEVC decoder instead of the
Store extension packages, so CanMfDecodeCodec returns true while Store
package paths are empty.

Skip the test when running on Windows versions earlier than WIN10_RS3.
This eliminates deterministic failures on win10-1507-tests-x64.

Extract tab separator helpers for tab group headers

Tab group headers need to paint separators the same way tabs do: when
two or more collapsed groups are next to each other, no visible tab can paint the separator between them.

Expose HorizontalTabStyleViews' separator bounds, painting, color, visible-background and hover-opacity logic as static helpers, and add TabGroupStyle::GetSeparatorOpacities() for group headers. No behavior change; the helpers are used in a follow-up CL (https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8805506)

Reuse precomputed download digest in FileAnalysisRequestBase

Previously, FileAnalysisRequestBase ignored the set digest and re-read
the entire file from disk to compute SHA-256 (overwriting unobfuscated
download hashes with obfuscated on-disk hashes and clearing digests for
large files when async hash computation was enabled).

Requests that open their file immediately now pass any digest set before
GetRequestData() to GetFileDataBlocking(), which reuses it once the file
is verified to be readable and non-empty. Requests that delay opening
their file (Save Package and upload/transfer flows) do not set a digest
beforehand and keep hashing from disk.

[SafeBrowsing] Move image-embedding model buffer in Scorer

Scorer::ApplyImageEmbeddingTfLiteModelHelper accepted model_data by
const std::string&, causing std::move(model_data) to fall back to
copying the 6.4 MB TFLite model buffer. CreateImageEmbedder then copied
model_data a second time when passing it to set_file_content().

Pass model_data by value in ApplyImageEmbeddingTfLiteModelHelper and
move it into set_file_content() in CreateImageEmbedder, matching the
classifier path and avoiding ~13 MB of redundant transient heap copies
during embedder initialization.

[FedCM] Return early in ShowErrorDialog() if the view destroys it

Previously, IdentityDialogController::ShowErrorDialog() modified member
state and notified the embedder whenever AccountSelectionView's
ShowErrorDialog() returned true, even if the view dismissed the dialog
synchronously and destroyed the controller. Now, ShowErrorDialog()
checks a WeakPtr after calling into the view and returns false if the
controller was destroyed, instead of using freed memory.

Add a unit test verifying that destroying the controller inside
ShowErrorDialog() returns false without accessing member state or
notifying the embedder.

The ghost loader showed a static placeholder in place of the close
button. If the expanded LHS iframe never loaded, the user could not
close the rail.

Replace the placeholder with a cr-icon-button that uses the Google
Symbols 2 side_nav icon (wght 200, opsz 24, FILL 0). Clicking it fires
close-rail, and <cr-left-hand-side> folds the rail. If the iframe loads
later, the rail stays folded.

view, and is inert otherwise like the other views. The decorative
placeholders stay aria-hidden; only the close button is exposed.

8d2010eb7979631f829e0311ccb634168895ab90 [ diff ] 
Make the thread cache dumps own their partition's buckets

The slots cached in PartitionAlloc's thread caches are already in the
resident size of their partition's buckets. When buckets are dumped,
the thread_cache dumps also carried those bytes as their size, so
summing a partition's children counted them twice, inflating the size
and effective_size of the partition, malloc/partitions and malloc.

Make the thread_cache dump own the partition's buckets dump, so it keeps
its size (read by the Malloc.ThreadCache UMA) without counting twice.
Owning the partition dump itself instead loses effective size, as
malloc/allocated_objects/partitions already owns malloc/partitions.

Background dumps have no buckets, so they get no edge.

android: Analyze lint per library

## wnwen (human)

This should unblock removing the build server, there are other perf
changes I have that improve lint further, but even as is (see the
agent's table below), it should be fast enough in each case to not be
the long pole in most builds, as if a build is adding new methods, its
java build will take more time too.

## Agent generated details

An apk's lint step analyzes all of its sources in one lint.py run
(139.4 s median for chrome_public_apk with native lint on a 48-core
machine), so a change to any one dependency re-runs all of it.

Analyze lint per Android library instead, and merge the partial results
in each apk's lint step. Incremental builds then re-analyze only the
libraries whose sources or dependency APIs changed. The result is mixed
but mostly a large win: every edit below is 2.6x to 35x faster, at 5x
the CPU when every lint action re-runs.

Build time of chrome_public_apk__lint after one edit, mean of the edit
and revert builds, native lint, 48-core machine (lint actions run in
brackets; measured before crrev.com/c/8675646 landed,
lint 32.6.0-alpha03, with crrev.com/c/8675583). Analysis stamps then
changed only with the partial results; they are now always touched,
which adds the report step (1.0 s, one more action) to each row:

  edit                         today     this CL
  comment, omnibox .java       127.6 s   12.8 s (1)
  comment, ChromeTabbedAct.    126.6 s   23.8 s (8)
  comment, base Log.java       133.2 s    3.8 s (1)
  new method, Log.java         138.6 s   52.8 s (489)
  new method, omnibox .java    130.3 s   26.6 s (17)
  comment, omnibox res .xml    134.6 s   27.2 s (1)

Re-running every lint action of chrome_public_apk takes 64.1 s and
1124 s of CPU, against 126.4 s and 223 s for the single native step
(CPU varied from 949 s to 1322 s over three runs; same 186 issues).

Each Android library with sources gets a __lint_analysis action that
writes partial lint results with the modes of crrev.com/c/8676999.
lint.py splits a large library across parallel lint processes by source
size, like Error Prone: one shard per 1MB, at most 8 and at most half
the usable CPUs (chrome_java: 8; 5 other libraries: 2). All shards of a
library re-run together: a comment in ChromeTabbedActivity.java re-runs
chrome_java's analysis in 13.3 s and 93 s of CPU, against 10.5 s and
11 s of CPU when each shard was its own GN action. Re-running every
lint action is unchanged (81.4 s and 1618 s of CPU, against 88.6 s and
1613 s). One sample each. The lint step of an apk
becomes two actions: __app_analysis for resources and sources of
non-analyzed targets, then a report step that merges all partial
results. __lint_partials groups collect the analysis targets of an
apk's transitive deps, next to __assetres and __header. All three kinds
of action run the native image and read the unpacked .aar dirs.

Each analyzed library also gets a __lint_annotations_zip action that
extracts its typedefs into an annotations.zip (0.7 s median and 11.5 s
for chrome_java during a full lint rebuild). Analyses read the zips of
their analyzed dependencies (sharded libraries also their own), and
__app_analysis those of the apk's analyzed libraries; __lint_annotations
groups collect them. A typedef file edit that leaves the zip unchanged
re-runs no dependent: a comment in base's ActivityState.java now re-runs
2 lint actions in 6.1 s, against 34 analyses in 29.0 s when analyses
read the sources of typedef files instead. Re-running every lint action
takes the same CPU (1638 s, of which 317 s extraction, against 1640 s)
in less time (86.9 s against 105.8 s for the lint actions). One sample
each.

Lint has one path. The "full" mode of lint.py, --use-build-server,
--cache-dir and --target-name are removed, and lint no longer goes to
the build server: with android_static_analysis="build_server" (the
default for non-official builds), lint now runs in the build and fails
it, where it ran after the build before. Every lint-enabled apk runs
__app_analysis and the report step. Apks with a custom lint_jar_path,
min_sdk_version or target_sdk_version do not merge library results,
since those come from the default lint jar and SDK versions
(cast_browser_apk, min SDK 24, otherwise fails on ObsoleteSdkInt from
its libraries): their __app_analysis analyzes all sources.

Analyses re-run for API changes of direct deps only, like turbine
(--depfile-classpath is the turbine interface classpath). With the
transitive classpath, building 30 upstream commits on top of a warm out
dir re-ran 375 of chrome_public_apk's 692 analyses; with direct deps,
58.

AnnotateVersionCheck runs on libraries since crrev.com/c/8676999 and
flags five SDK_INT helpers in chrome_java and omnibox, which
crrev.com/c/8825032 annotates; this CL is based on it.

Library analyses on the native image get a 512M heap instead of 2G,
which grows by 200MB per MB of source in the shard, up to 2G.
Re-running every lint action takes the same time (80.0 s against
82.7 s) with a lower peak RSS per analysis (705 MB against 2075 MB at
most, 534 MB against 622 MB median); 256M takes 17% more CPU. Machines
with fewer than 16 CPUs get fewer, larger shards of chrome_java: its 4
shards of 5MB (8 CPUs) take 17.2 s with 512M, 15.8 s with 1G and 16.0 s
with 2G; its 2 shards of 10MB (4 CPUs) take 42.8 s, 25.8 s and 24.5 s.
JVM hosts start at 1G: with 512M the chrome_java analysis takes 58 s
instead of 30 s, and 1G matches 2G for the full run (257 s against
262 s, 8247 s against 8319 s of CPU).

testonly libraries get no __lint_analysis. Bots build "all", which
otherwise runs analyses that no apk lint step needs: android_compile_dbg
ran 1117 analyses, 368 with "test" in the label. Locally this cuts
analysis targets from 1168 to 813; chrome_public_apk needs 692.

This changes lint on every Android bot that runs it
(android_compile_dbg, cast, cronet). Not measured: machines with fewer
cores, and the steady state of a bot whose out dir lags by many commits
(with JVMs, 100 commits re-ran 500 analyses for one base_java API
change: 6510 s of lint CPU instead of 389 s). On hosts other than
linux-x64, lint runs on JVMs, where per-library analysis is slower than
a single step for an API change in base (195.8 s against 156.2 s) and a
full run takes 250.1 s and 7435 s of CPU.

Remove 2-arg TabReparentingParams constructor

TabReparentingParams had a 2-argument convenience constructor that
forwarded to the 3-argument one with a null source TabModelSelector.
Delete it so the class has a single constructor, and update all callers
to pass `/* sourceSelector= */ null` explicitly.

The intent is to make every caller state explicitly whether detaching
from a source TabModelSelector is deferred, instead of silently getting
the no-selector behavior from an overload. This costs some extra lines
at call sites that pass null, several of which now wrap.

No behavior change: every updated call site passes exactly the null the
removed overload passed.

Don't dirty slot assignment from UA manual slotting [2/8]

Design doc: go/fixing-slot-assignment-recalc

The user-agent shadow trees of <details>, <select>, and <optgroup> use
manual slotting. Their ManuallyAssignSlots() runs from inside slot
assignment recalc, and called HTMLSlotElement::Assign(), which is the
implementation of the author-facing assign(). Assign() marks the shadow
root's slot assignment dirty and signals a slot change (enqueueing a
slotchange event and re-checking slot changes), all from inside the
recalc that is computing that same assignment. This violates rule R4 in
slot_assignment.h (recalc does not dirty slot assignment).

This CL adds HTMLSlotElement::SetManuallyAssignedNodesForRecalc(),
which only updates the slot's manually assigned nodes. The one side
effect that is still needed, invalidating :has-slotted, is recorded and
applied from DidRecalcAssignedNodes(), after the assignment has been
computed. The UA ManuallyAssignSlots() implementations now use it.

[Android] Replace ProfileIntentUtils with ProfileTokenUtils

ProfileTokenUtils carries a Profile through intents, PendingIntents and
notifications using a single representation: the bytes of the Profile's
ProfileResolver token, encoded as URL-safe base64. The serialized proto
bytes are passed between C++ and Java as a byte[], avoiding UTF-8 String
conversion on arbitrary protobuf wire bytes. It is stable across
restarts and differs between Profiles, including between a regular
Profile and its off-the-record Profiles.

Beyond the existing addProfileToIntent(), hasProfileToken() and
retrieveProfileFromIntent(), it adds typed helpers for per-Profile state
outside the Profile, so that features behave correctly with multiple
Profiles without handling the token themselves:
- setProfileScopedIdentity() makes PendingIntents for different
  Profiles distinct.
- getNotificationTag() returns a per-Profile notification tag, and
  getNotificationTagFromIntent() returns the same tag from an intent
  without native, e.g. to dismiss the notification from a receiver.

Intents now carry the encoded token under a new extra. Intents posted
before this change carry the raw token under the old extra; those are
still read until M163.

All ProfileIntentUtils callers are migrated and ProfileIntentUtils is
removed. Since encoded tokens are persisted, ProfileToken documents that
its serialized form must not change, and a native test pins it.

[TTC] Keep the offline indicator from showing in TTC browser tests

On Android, a device that is offline shows an indicator above the page
a couple of seconds after startup, and test devices and emulators are
usually offline. The indicator changes the height of the top controls
and resizes the page's view in the middle of a test. That has made TTC
browser tests flaky twice: crbug.com/574927722 and crbug.com/585984040.

Two fixtures passed --force-online-connection-state-for-indicator for
that reason, each with its own copy of the explanation. Pass it in
TtcCoreBrowserTestBase instead, so that every fixture derived from it
gets it, and remove the copies.

PointerInputObserverBrowserTest now derives from TtcCoreBrowserTestBase
too, which also replaces its own setup of the test server.
TtcKeyedServiceBrowserTest stays as it is: it tests whether the real
service is created, with the feature in several states, and does not
use the page.

PointerContextCapturerScaleBrowserTest still captures again when the
view was resized during a capture: on devices the view was also resized
by something other than the indicator.

On an Android 16 x64 emulator the view of that test used to shrink
about 2 s after startup (e.g. from 1440 px to 1377 px high). With this
change it keeps its size for 5 s after the test.

parent
456e08700f1960a3d5c4f7d123f02a16d4e8c368 [ diff ] 
[tips] Migrate the V1 channel to V2 instead of deleting it on upgrade

The V1 Tips channel ("tips") holds the user's opt-in decision: users
opted in by enabling it in system settings. M150 added it to
LEGACY_CHANNEL_IDS and copied it to "tips_v2" from the static
initializer of the lazily loaded PredefinedChannels. On upgrade,
ChannelsUpdater deleted the legacy channels before that class was
loaded, so the copy found nothing and V1 opt-ins were lost. The copy
was later removed, so upgrades from M149 or older still delete "tips"
without migrating it.

Move "tips" from LEGACY_CHANNEL_IDS to a new MIGRATED_LEGACY_CHANNELS
map (tips -> tips_v2). A new LegacyChannelMigrator runs as part of the
channel update and, from one channel snapshot, copies an enabled legacy
channel to its replacement (capped at the predefined importance, and
never overwriting an existing replacement) before deleting the legacy
channel. The channels version is now stored only after the migration
has run, so an interrupted update is retried.

[glic] Reset warming pool timestamp on cold start

When GlicWebContentsWarmingPool::TakeContainer() misses, it creates an
on-demand container via EnsurePreload(kUserTriggeredColdStart) to hand
back immediately. That call invoked OnWarmedContentCreated() and left
warmed_container_creation_time_ populated with the creation time of the
already-consumed container, causing subsequent misses before a refill
completed (such as kPendingBackfill) to emit spurious samples to
Glic{GlicProvider}.WarmingPool.TimeSinceCreatedAtMiss.

Skip setting warmed_container_creation_time_ for on-demand cold-start
creations and explicitly reset it when a container is handed out or on
shutdown, while preserving timestamps from unused pre-warmed containers
evicted by expiry, crash, load error, or memory pressure. Also drop the
obsolete provider-resolution comment in OnReloadAfterExpiry() and add
unit tests covering both suppressed and valid cases.

Add slot assignment recalc invariant checks [1/8]

Design doc: go/fixing-slot-assignment-recalc

Slot assignment is recalculated lazily, and today nothing stops recalc
side effects from running script, dispatching events, mutating the DOM,
moving focus, or re-dirtying and re-entering slot assignment (see the
bug for example call chains). The existing guards are DCHECK-only, or
silently throw a JS exception (ScriptForbiddenScope).

This CL documents the rules (R1-R7, in the SlotAssignment class comment
and core/dom/README.md), and adds SlotAssignmentRecalcInProgressScope,
a global scope held during SlotAssignment::RecalcAssignment(). Checks
are added at the script, event, DOM mutation, focus, and slot-dirtying
entry points, at re-entrant or forbidden recalc, and where the lazy
flat tree entry points are used while flat tree traversal is forbidden.
SlotAssignmentRecalcForbiddenScope is now active in release builds.

The two scopes guard opposite directions:
SlotAssignmentRecalcForbiddenScope (per-document) marks code where the
tree is unstable, so a recalc must not start there (R5), while
SlotAssignmentRecalcInProgressScope marks a running recalc, and
restricts what the recalc and its side effects may do (R1-R4, R7).

SlotAssignmentRecalcInProgressScope also replaces
FlatTreeTraversalForbiddenScope (now
SlotAssignmentRecalcInProgressScope::ForbidFlatTreeTraversal) and
Document's slot assignment recalc depth counter (now
SlotAssignmentRecalcInProgressScope::IsActive()), both of which were
only set by slot assignment recalc. Both are now global instead of
per-document.

Reporting is a no-op in this CL, so there is no behavior change. The
known violators are fixed in follow-up CLs, and reporting is enabled
after that.

ScrollIntoViewBrowserTest.EditableInLocalRoot is flaking across Linux
CI and try builders (over 400 flaky verdicts per variant in the past 3
days), timing out in ScopedFocusScrollWaiter::RunLoop::Run() and
occasionally failing the initial viewport.page_left check, matching
the existing Linux timeout in EditableInDoublyNestedFrame.

Example failure: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8664869418480392417

[TabbedCCT] Add per-app/per-account state directory and metadata retirement

Define EXTRA_TABBED_CCT_ACCOUNT_ID in CustomTabIntentDataProvider and
require both a verified client package name and an account ID extra for
Tabbed CCT to be enabled.

When Tabbed CCT is enabled for a CustomTabActivity:
- Store tab persistence files in an isolated per-app, per-account
  directory under custom_tabs_app/app_<packageName>/
  acct_<sha256_16(accountId)>. When the account ID does not exist,
  acct_default/ is used.
- Name the live activity's metadata file with the "tab_state_active_"
  prefix (tab_state_active_<taskId>_<uuid>).
- On activity finish (excluding reparenting / open-in-browser), save tab
  state and rename the active metadata file to
  tab_state_retired_<taskId>_<uuid>_<timestamp> instead of deleting the
  tabs and metadata file.

For now, the retired metadata file remains unclaimed. Will be merged to
a newly introduced one hosting all the closed tabs in a follow-up
change.

Remove Windows 11 24H2 check for enhanced security event fields

IsEnhancedSecurityEventFieldsEnabled() turned off enhanced security
event fields on Windows 11 24H2+ because the network name query made
synchronous WLAN API calls that could hang the UI thread.
GetNetworkName() no longer makes those calls on Windows 11 24H2+, so the
extra check now only drops fields that are safe to collect, such as the
device FQDN. Remove it so kEnhancedSecurityEventFields applies on
Windows 11 24H2+ again.

Webium: set window creation sources in //chrome/browser/ui

Previously, several normal browser window creation paths in
`//chrome/browser/ui` did not set a window creation source on
`InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager`, leaving their creation source as
`kUnknown`.

This CL switches those callers to
`waap::CreateBrowserWindowAndRecordCreationSource()`:
- `kSessionRestore` in `BrowserLiveTabContext::Create()`, with browser
  test coverage in `InitialWebUIWindowCreationSourceBrowserTest`.
- `kDragToNewWindow` in `TabDragWindowAdapterImpl::DetachToNewWindow()`.
- `kMoveTabsToNewWindow` in `BrowserTabStripModelDelegate` and
  `AiOverlayTools::ExecuteWorkspaceSubAgentOutput()`.
- `kNavigation` in `bookmark_menu_cocoa_controller.mm`,
  `OmniboxEverywhereService`, and `ChromeWebContentsHandler`.
- `kLaunch` in `OpenApplicationTab()` (`application_launch.cc`) and
  `WebAppLaunchProcess::CreateBrowserForLaunch()`.
- `kNewEmptyWindow` in `browser_mac.cc`, `chrome_pages.cc`, and
  `window_applescript.mm`.

Remove AIManager::MaybeTryEagerInit()

Eager initialization in AIManager::MaybeTryEagerInit() requested assets
for other Built-in AI features whenever one feature succeeded, assuming
each feature needed a separate configuration download. Now that feature
configurations live in the manifest component, other features become
available automatically with the common model, and eager requests only
make per-feature usage tracking data less accurate.

Remove MaybeTryEagerInit(), kBuiltInAIEagerInit, and tried_init_.

Certificate viewer: Show a readable title for MTC CA certificates

MTC CA names consist of a single id-rdna-trustAnchorID attribute with a
RELATIVE-OID value and no common name, so GetTitle() fell back to the
RFC 2253 form, e.g. "1.3.6.1.5.5.7.25.3=#82DB4E030103", in the
certificate hierarchy. Title these certificates as
"trustAnchorID=44494.3.1.3" instead.

In the future, this title will display the MTC CA's friendly_name, but
that requires further plumbing. Show a slightly more readable string in
the meantime.

GetTitle() is shared with iOS, so this also moves the trustAnchorID
label to the shared OID string table in components/certificate_model,
and the UI string to the appropriate grd file.

[WebUI Toolbar] Report every location icon press, like native

The WebUI location icon ignored presses while it was unclickable, e.g.
while the omnibox is being edited, when it is empty, or when it shows
the Google logo. It only tracked them for drags, which close the omnibox
popup, so Linux middle-click paste-and-go did not work. Native Views
reports every press of the icon and only blocks the click that would
open Page Info.

Do the same in the WebUI: report every press, whether or not the icon is
clickable, and keep blocking Page Info in the click handler while it is
unclickable. Drag handling is unchanged.

This means left and right presses on an unclickable icon now also send a
Mojo message, which the browser currently ignores. That is intentional:
the browser, not the WebUI, should decide what a press does, and one
message per press is negligible. Native also uses these presses for
features the WebUI doesn't have yet, such as opening the omnibox context
menu on press while the AI Mode popup is open.

[Toolbar] Pass unfocusedAlpha to TintObserver#onTintChanged

Plumb float unfocusedAlpha (derived from R.dimen.default_disabled_alpha
when the activity is unfocused, or 1.0f when focused) through
ThemeColorProvider.TintObserver#onTintChanged so observers can dim
elements when the activity is unfocused without querying activity focus
state directly.

A separate alpha value is needed alongside activityFocusTint because
applying a monochrome tint (SRC_IN) to full-color bitmap icons (such as
extension action icons or signed-in profile avatars) would overwrite
their original colors.

[BrowserView] Return WebContents size from GetContentsSize()

GetContentsSize() returns the size of the active ContentsContainerView,
which also contains the NTP footer, docked DevTools and the split view
border. E.g. with the NTP footer visible, it's 57px taller than the
WebContents.

On Linux, this trips a DCHECK in LoadRestoredTabIfVisible() when
restoring a window whose active tab shows the NTP footer (e.g. session
restore or Ctrl+Shift+T on a closed window). AddRestoredTabImpl()
resizes the tab to GetContentsSize(), then activates the window, which
on Linux shows it (crrev.com/c/8760984) and lays the tab back out to its
real size before the DCHECK compares the two.

Return the active ContentsWebView's size instead, matching the
BrowserWindow::GetContentsSize() comment and what it returned before
crrev.com/c/6771233. SetContentsSize() now sizes the WebContents rather
than its container, so ResizesInSplitView checks ContentsWebView sizes.

Repro: with the NTP footer showing, press Ctrl+N, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Shift+W,
then Ctrl+Shift+T.

[Test] Deflake SiteSearchTest#testSiteSearchTriggeredByTab

testSiteSearchTriggeredByTab kept a reference to a suggestion row view
and polled it for the selected state. A width change can recycle that
view, and recycled rows are deselected while the selection moves to the
newly bound row, so the test timed out on loaded tablet emulators.
OmniboxTestUtils.checkSuggestionSelected() now also checks the row view
currently bound to the index on every poll, and the test uses it. The
only other caller,
OmniboxTest#testTabSelectsFirstSuggestionUpdatesUrlBarText, now gets the
stricter check too.

[tabstrip_ntb] Bypass renderer URL loader throttles for the NTB on Android

On desktop, Top Chrome WebUI renderers skip creating URL loader
throttles for their resource requests, gated by the
WebUIReloadButtonBypassLoaderThrottles param. The bypass was compiled
out on Android, so the NTB renderer still created the full set of
throttles for every subresource, including those served in-process.

Add the Android-only AndroidTopChromeWebUIBypassLoaderThrottles feature
to gate the same bypass for Top Chrome WebUI renderers on Android, and
add it to the AndroidNewTabButtonTabstripWebUI study. Desktop behavior
is unchanged.

parent
3563d4b5cf1a236b4c3d132b864e7d3e775b678c [ diff ] 
grit: Add zstd as a compression option

zstd decompresses faster than gzip and brotli, with a compression
ratio between the two, which makes it a good fit for resources that
are decompressed at runtime (e.g. WebUI).

Adds compress="zstd" to grit, with an optional compression level via
compress="zstdN" (e.g. "zstd19", "zstd22", or "zstd-2" for negative
"fast" levels). Targets that use it must set "use_zstd = true", which
uses a new host-only zstd CLI target in //third_party/zstd.

Unlike brotli, no custom header is needed, since zstd frames start
with a magic number and grit stores the decompressed size in the frame
header.

[Masonry] Add cross-track reading flow

Gating `reading-flow: grid-lanes-flow` behind a new flag, per CSSWG
resolution [1] that this portion should not ship until it has received
spec feedback.

Implementing `reading-flow: grid-lanes-flow` in a fashion very close
to the strongest proposal in that Issue [2], but with minor adjustments
and simplification.
- Make a "reading row" comprised by the "next" item in each lane.
- Make a "reading region" that extends to the end of the furthest-out
item in the reading row.
- Iterate through the lanes, starting with the "next" item used to make
the reading region, and keep including items from that lane until
encountering an item that has more than 1/3 of itself sticking out past
the end of the reading region. Don't include that item

This notably does not include stopping early if the lane feels
sufficiently full, as that is still a very contentious part of the
proposal that complicates the implementation. It can be added later if
it becomes agreed upon.

[1] https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/5675
[2] https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/5675#issuecomment-4848519759

[PWA] Isolate internal launch parameters

Some internal web-app launches build their parameters from Chrome's
startup command line. This can cause a later launch to inherit the
original shortcut URL or be attributed to OS login. Construct fresh
AppLaunchParams so these launches use only their own input.

WebApp.LaunchSource changes from kFromCommandLine or kFromOsLogin to
kFromChromeInternal by default. This also affects DevTools PWA.launch,
chrome://iwa-dev, and the IWA intent picker. IWA navigation capture uses
kFromNavigationCapturing, the post-install fallback launch uses
kFromInstaller. Explicit caller sources remain unchanged.

This also avoids carrying an old Linux activation token into these
launches when token forwarding is added in a follow-up CL.

Move DidCommitDocumentReplacement to blink::mojom::LocalFrameHost

Move the DidCommitDocumentReplacement IPC from content.mojom.FrameHost
to blink.mojom.LocalFrameHost. This allows Blink's DocumentLoader to
call the browser directly on document replacement commits (e.g.
javascript: URLs, XSLT transforms, or discarded frames) rather than
routing through WebLocalFrameClient and RenderFrameImpl.

performance_manager: Defer background tab loads while visible page loads

This CL defers initiating restored background tab loads in
`BackgroundTabLoadingPolicy::GetMaxNewTabLoads()` while any visible page
is tracked in `page_nodes_loading_` (`kLoading` or `kLoadedBusy` prior
to CPU/network quiescence, capped at 15s per contiguous visible-loading
window via `kMaxVisibleLoadingDeferralTimeout`), gated behind
`kDeferBackgroundTabLoadsWhileVisiblePageLoads`. If a loading visible
page is hidden early, `OnIsVisibleChanged()` posts `MaybeLoadSomeTabs()`
asynchronously so synchronous foreground tab switches do not transiently
unblock background tab loads before the incoming tab starts loading.

During multi-tab session restore on >= 4-core devices (2-4 simultaneous
loading slots, reaching the 4-slot cap on >= 8 cores),
`GetMaxNewTabLoads()` previously returned available background loading
slots before `Startup.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint`, causing background tab
navigations and renderer commits on `CrBrowserMain` to contend with the
foreground tab and InitialWebUI toolbar.

Populated-profile 5-tab `--restore-last-session` Crossbench A/B
(paired P50 (median) delta and bot-clustered 95% CI):
- Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3:
  Local Linux (`N=32`) -45.0 ms / -4.82% ([-87.0, -15.0] ms, P90 -142ms)
  Pinpoint Linux (`N=98`) -38.0 ms / -9.82% ([-47.0, -22.0] ms)
  Pinpoint Mac (`N=99`) -12.0 ms / -2.77% ([-22.0, -8.0] ms)
  Pinpoint Win10 (`N=55`) -68.0 ms / -2.79% ([-135.0, +6.0] ms)
- Startup.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint:
  Local Linux (`N=32`) -42.0 ms / -5.55% ([-74.0, -11.0] ms, P90 -146ms)
  Pinpoint Linux (`N=100`) -13.5 ms / -5.71% ([-15.0, -5.0] ms)
  Pinpoint Win10 (`N=90`) -20.0 ms / -1.97% ([-38.0, +7.0] ms)
- InitialWebUI.Startup.SessionRestore.ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint:
  Local Linux (`N=32`) -40.0 ms / -4.09% ([-94.0, -7.0] ms, P90 -121ms)
  Pinpoint Mac (`N=100`) -5.0 ms / -1.32% ([-9.0, -2.0] ms)
  Pinpoint Linux (`N=100`) -17.0 ms / -5.53% ([-28.0, +2.0] ms)
- SessionRestore.ForegroundTabFirstPaint4:

[Composebox] Add an SRP URL type for composebox queries

Composebox query URLs can currently only be built for AI Mode or Lens
results. This adds SearchUrlType::kSrp and GetUrlForContextualSrp() so
a later CL can send composebox queries to the Search results page
instead.

The kSrp URL is the AI Mode URL without `udm` or `lns_mode=cvst`: it
keeps `aep`, `amc` and `aai`, and always sends attachments as `cinpts`
(with their upload type, even for one file) plus `gsessionid` and
`lns_surface`. Unlike AI Mode, it waits for in-flight uploads even when
non-blocking URL navigation is enabled. Without valid context (text
only, or an expired session) it falls back to a Search results page URL
without context rather than AI Mode.

GetUrlForMultimodalSearch() now appends its context params through a
helper shared with GetUrlForContextualSrp(); its output is unchanged.

Nothing creates kSrp URLs yet.

[Omnibox] Switch UrlBar IME between URL and natural text for AI Mode

Behind the OmniboxUrlBarAimNaturalTextIme feature flag, UrlBarMediator
now observes AutocompleteInput#getRequestTypeSupplier() and updates
UrlBarProperties.USE_NATURAL_TEXT_IME whenever the session transitions
between conventional requests and AI Mode fulfillments.

When natural text IME is active, UrlBar configures
onCreateInputConnection() for natural text composition (clearing
TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_NO_SUGGESTIONS, omitting TYPE_TEXT_VARIATION_URI, and
enabling TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_AUTO_CORRECT and TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_SENTENCES)
so soft keyboards show ',' instead of '/' and enable
composition/autocorrect. When transitioning between conventional and
AI Mode, UrlBar calls InputMethodManager#restartInput() if active so
the keyboard updates immediately.

parent
963f74359908028b40f57d465759b9ae3f58b972 [ diff ] 
[iOS] Record Secure Gateway routing metrics

ProxyServiceController now records the Secure Gateway routing rules it
gives to WebKit's proxy configuration, in new
Enterprise.SecureGateway.Routing.* histograms:

- RuleCount: the number of rules given to ProxyConfigurationProvider.
- MatchDomainCount: the total number of destination matchers (domains,
  IP addresses and subnets) of these rules.
- UnsupportedRuleCount: the number of rules that the translation leaves
  out because none of their proxies is supported by WebKit, e.g. SOCKS5
  only. They were only logged so far.

EnterpriseProxyService notifies its observers when a route refresh
starts and completes, about every 10 minutes, usually with unchanged
routes. So the controller keeps the last rules it gave to the provider
and the number of rules left out, and only records the metrics when
they change: when routes are first fetched or restored from the cache,
when they are updated, and when they are removed (0 rules). Comparing
the number of rules left out too records the configs where WebKit
supports none of the rules, which leave WebKit without rules. Profiles
without routes record nothing, so the client count of RuleCount above 0
gives the number of clients with routing active.

Like routing itself, the metrics are only recorded on iOS 18.1+.

Build the snap package on linux-rel

Adds `checkout_snap_runtime` to `gclient_gn_args` and makes it the
default of the `enable_snap_package` GN arg on x64, as
`use_bundled_mutter` does with `checkout_mutter`. Builds in a checkout
with the snap runtime then build the snap package along with the .deb
and .rpm packages.

Applies the new `checkout_snap_runtime` gclient config to `Linux
Builder`, which `linux-rel` mirrors, so the CI and the CQ build the
snap package. `GPU Linux Builder` gets it too because `linux-rel`
mirrors both builders and their gclient configs have to match.

The bot images have mksquashfs since squashfs-tools was added to
install-build-deps.py (crrev.com/c/8708672).

[ash] input_method: test the editor's connection to the Orca service

No test reached EditorMediator::ResetEditorConnections(). That is
where the mediator connects to the Orca service and gives the user's
AccountId to EditorSystemActuator. The connection is made by
EditorServiceConnector, which launches the Orca service process, and
unit tests cannot launch it.

EditorServiceConnector::SetLaunchOverrideForTesting() lets a test
provide an in-process service instead, for as long as the test keeps
the returned base::AutoReset. Without an override the connector
launches the service process as before.

The new unit test focuses a text field, which connects the mediator
to a mock Orca service. The test then submits feedback the way the
service does, and checks that the feedback is sent with the Orca
product id for the account of the profile.

[remoting] Parallelize ARGB-to-NV12 conversion in WebrtcVideoEncoderGpu

Adds `ConvertDesktopFrameToNv12()` in `remoting/codec/utils` and adopts
it in `WebrtcVideoEncoderGpu::Core::Encode()` (using span-safe
`VideoFrame::GetWritableVisiblePlaneData()`), replacing single-threaded
full-frame `libyuv::ARGBToNV12()`.

Shares `GetMaxParallelWorkers()`, even-row horizontal strip splitting,
and `RunStripsInParallel()` (`base::CreateJob(...).Join()`) with
`ConvertDesktopFrameRegionToYuv()`, parallelizing full-frame NV12
conversion on frames >= 512,000 pixels across disjoint 2x2 subsampled
UV rows while draining inline if `ThreadPool` workers are contended.

Measured in a release `remoting_unittests` microbenchmark (`is_debug =
false`, `dcheck_always_on = false`; 200 interleaved A/B/B/A iterations
of `ConvertDesktopFrameToNv12()` vs `libyuv::ARGBToNV12()` on a
48-core Intel Xeon, since `WebrtcVideoEncoderGpu` is not wired into
`webrtc_video_encoder_benchmark`):
- 8 workers (`kMaxWorkers` default): -61% at 1080p (542 -> 210 us),
  -72% at 1440p (1,083 -> 303 us), and -81% at 4K (2.98 -> 0.56 ms).
- 2 workers (4-core cap, `ScopedParallelConversionCpuCapForTesting(2)`
  with `taskset -c 0-3`): -24% at 1080p (474 -> 360 us), -36% at 1440p
  (923 -> 591 us), and -46% at 4K (2.92 -> 1.58 ms).
- Saturated `ThreadPool` (`ScopedSaturateForegroundThreadPool`):
  matches single-threaded latency without queue stalls (488 -> 489 us
  at 1080p; 3.28 -> 3.25 ms at 4K).

parent
8ba0556aca84e6077ce0efdb134982a8b50b6866 [ diff ] 
[Toolbar] Check captured bitmap height when moving toolbar to bottom

Leaving a customized-color NTP while the toolbar is anchored at the top
removes the status bar top padding and shrinks the control container
view back to its unpadded height. However, `ToolbarViewResourceAdapter`
blocks a new capture while browser controls are locked, such as during a
tab switch or on an error page.

Moving the address bar to the bottom in that state sees no layout or
container height change, even though the compositor still holds the
padded NTP bitmap and draws it above the bottom toolbar.

We now also check the height of the last captured toolbar bitmap so
moving the toolbar to the bottom forces a synchronous layout and capture
whenever the bitmap is still padded.

After: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qJtQi6DOQkjEOAgaTsxAxxLFRMLrogGg/view

testFirstTextViewInPassphraseDialogNotReceivingFocus and

[OmniboxEverywhere] Respect background and startup enterprise policies

Omnibox Everywhere previously kept Chrome running in the background
and registered background launch on OS startup based solely on its own
preferences, even when enterprise administrators disabled background
mode or launch on startup.

This CL updates Omnibox Everywhere to respect the background mode and
launch on startup prefs when they are managed and disabled by
enterprise policy, including dynamic updates, so background execution
and startup launch are turned off when disallowed by policy.

[geic] Handle Workforce Auth Portal redirects in guest throttle

On .google.com Gemini Enterprise hosts, an unauthenticated request to
/side-panel still serves HTTP 200 so the web client can load, render a
sign-in prompt, and open a pop-out sign-in tab. By contrast, Workforce
Identity hosts (*.cloud.google, *.gemini-us.google, and
business.gemini.google) require a session-index query parameter
(csesidx) on the URL. Because the configured GeminiEnterpriseUrl policy
URL has no csesidx, a cold side-panel load receives an HTTP 302 redirect
to the paired Workforce Auth Portal
(auth.{cloud,business.gemini,gemini-us}.google) before the web client
can load. Previously, GlicGuestNavigationThrottle and
PwcNavigationThrottle rejected that redirect as kOriginBlocked, showing
the generic error panel ("Something went wrong") even when the user was
already signed in on another tab.

When the user already has a single active session in the browser (or is
refreshing an existing session), non-interactive endpoints on the paired
Auth Portal (/select-session, /account-chooser, /refreshcookies,
/submit) do not render a document; they immediately 302-redirect back to
the Gemini Enterprise origin with csesidx=<N>. When interactive sign-in
or account selection is required, the Auth Portal either redirects to
/signin*, /login*, /reauth*, or an external/1P IdP, or returns a 200 OK
HTML page—which must be completed in a pop-out browser tab rather than
inside PrivilegedWebContents.

To support both cases without ever committing an Auth Portal document or
granting Glic Mojo API access to auth.<domain>.google:
- Allow 302 redirect transit through the Workforce Auth Portal origin
  paired with GetGuestURL() in IsGuestOriginAllowed() (gated on
  kGlicDisconnectedWebview), while keeping IsOriginAllowedGlicApi()
  false.
- In GlicGuestNavigationThrottle, allow non-interactive 302 hops on the
  paired Auth Portal to proceed so already-signed-in users resolve
  csesidx=<N> automatically, while cancelling interactive sign-in
  redirects (/signin*, /login*, /reauth*), redirects after the Auth
  Portal to non-guest origins (3P or 1P IdPs), and any terminal HTTP
  response on the Auth Portal (via WillProcessResponse()) via
  OnGuestNavigationBlocked(GuestPageType::kSignInRequired, url).
- Add GeicSignInController (enabled when GlicProviderSpec::
  UsesGeicSignIn() is true) to own the pop-out GeicManagedTab,
  SignInObserver, and csesidx resolution, transitioning
  GlicNoWebviewContentsManager to ErrorPanelType::kSignIn on
  kSignInRequired and reloading the guest with csesidx=<N> once sign-in
  completes.

[A11y] Use author-provided names for unplayable media elements

Previously, AccessibilityMediaElement::TextAlternative() checked
IsUnplayable() (`networkState == NETWORK_EMPTY || NETWORK_NO_SOURCE` or
a playback error) before calling AXNodeObject::TextAlternative(), and
returned the localized IDS_MEDIA_PLAYBACK_ERROR string ("Unable to play
media.") whenever the media element wasn't ready to play.

Because that check ran before standard accessible name computation, any
`<video>` or `<audio>` without a loaded source—including lazy-loaded
videos or elements still waiting on network—ignored author-supplied
`aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, and `title` attributes. It also left
`name_from` unset (so `title` was exposed again as the accessible
description and DevTools showed no name sources) and leaked "Unable to
play media." into ancestor names computed from content, such as
`<a><video></video>Watch</a>`.

Remove the `AccessibilityMediaElement::TextAlternative()` override so
media elements always go through `AXNodeObject::TextAlternative()`,
matching HTML-AAM, WebKit, and Gecko. Unplayable media elements still
expose `kRestrictionDisabled` via `AccessibilityMediaElement::Restriction()`
and keep their media controls disabled.

Also remove the IDS_MEDIA_PLAYBACK_ERROR string from blink_strings.grd,
which no longer has any users.

AX-Relnotes: Unplayable <video> and <audio> elements now take their
accessible name from the author (aria-labelledby, aria-label, title)
instead of always being named "Unable to play media.".

Add BatchProgressTracker to track sequential ("1 of 3" -> "2 of 3" -> "3
of 3") progress across a tab's queued infobars. Attach it to
InfoBarManager via base::SupportsUserData so batch progress survives tab
switches, background-tab removals, and moving a tab to a new window.

RemoveInfoBarInternal/ReplaceInfoBarInternal's documented contract when
multiple observers are attached.

follow-up CL.

parent
85f62f563ca5dc04334853a257cfed9aa19dad42 [ diff ] 
[DevTools] Resume a target waiting for debugger when detaching from it

A target that is auto-attached with waitForDebuggerOnStart stays paused
until the client sends Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger. When the client
detaches from the session without resuming it first, nothing can resume
the target anymore, so it should continue running. This already works
for dedicated workers, but the following targets were left paused
forever:

- Out-of-process iframes. The navigation throttle was still waiting for
  the detached session. Detaching a session now releases its throttles.

- Service workers. Whether to pause a new worker on start is recorded
  when the agent host is created, and was used even when the session
  has been detached while the main script was being fetched. This is
  now ignored when no session is attached, similar to what is done for
  a restarted worker.

- Popups opened with window.open(). These are paused in the renderer
  together with the opener. The renderer was discarding the
  `session_waits_for_debugger` flag for frames, so the session had no
  V8 debugger barrier to release upon destruction. The flag is now
  passed through. As a result, a popup with multiple waiting sessions
  is resumed once all of them have been resumed or detached, as
  described in devtools_agent.mojom, and no longer by the first
  session to resume.

[remoting] Parameterize codec utils unit tests and add test helpers

Refactors `remoting/codec/utils_unittest.cc` so each test exercises a
single scenario using struct-parameterized `TEST_P` suites instead of
nested `for` loops and inline `is_i444` branching:
- Splits `GetBoundingRect` and `GetRowAlignedRegion` into
  single-scenario tests.
- Replaces `align`, `region`, and `is_i444` loops in
  `ConvertDesktopFrameRegionToYuv` tests with explicit parameter
  structs (`RegionAlignmentTestParam`, `RegionParallelTestParam`, and
  `YuvSubsamplingTestParam`).
- Extracts `ScopedSaturateForegroundThreadPool` to share saturated
  `ThreadPool` setup across conversion suites.
- Adds `ScopedParallelConversionCpuCapForTesting` so 1- and 2-vCPU CQ
  bots deterministically exercise the multi-strip `CreateJob` path.

Fix leak of DiscardsDetailsProviderImpl in chrome://discards

DiscardsDetailsProviderImpl is passed to the performance manager graph
when chrome://discards binds discards::mojom::DetailsProvider, but
nothing took it back when the pipe disconnected. Each load or reload of
chrome://discards therefore left one instance in the graph until
shutdown. This regressed in https://crrev.com/d7eaa73cc0273, which
replaced the DiscardsUI-owned unique_ptr with graph ownership.

Set a disconnect handler that takes the instance back from the graph,
which deletes it. SiteDataProviderImpl already does the same.

[FedCM] Rename multi-IDP flags on Android

Rename `mIsMultipleIdps` (`setIsMultipleIdps` and
`HeaderProperties.IS_MULTIPLE_IDPS`) to `mIsShowingMultipleIdps`
(`setIsShowingMultipleIdps` and
`HeaderProperties.IS_SHOWING_MULTIPLE_IDPS`), and
`mIsMultipleIdpsRequest` (`HeaderProperties.IS_MULTIPLE_IDPS_REQUEST`)
to `mIsMultiIdpRequest` (`HeaderProperties.IS_MULTI_IDP_REQUEST`), so
that the names say which one describes the current state of the dialog
and which one describes the request. None of the old names is reused, so
code written against them fails to compile instead of reading a
different value.

Also set `mIsShowingMultipleIdps` from `mIsMultiIdpRequest` on the
loading sheet, which has no accounts or IDPs to count, so that it
matches `HeaderProperties.IS_SHOWING_MULTIPLE_IDPS` there, and have
`createHeaderItem()` read the header type, IDP, RP context and multi-IDP
state from the members instead of taking them as parameters. No behavior
change: the loading sheet is only shown in active mode, and has no
accounts or login rows.

[glic] Advertise HostCapability::kExecuteJs

The Glic web client needs to know whether the host supports
isolated-world JavaScript execution for browser actuation before
exposing the corresponding tool.

Add kExecuteJs to mojom::HostCapability, regenerate
glic_api_generated.ts via
chrome/browser/resources/glic/glic_api_impl/generate.py, and emit
kExecuteJs in PopulateGlobalClientInitialState() when
actor::kActorExecuteJsTool (disabled by default) is enabled. This only
advertises client capability to the web client; browser-side execution
remains independently gated by actor::kActorExecuteJsTool in
actor_proto_conversion.cc.

Add unit and browser test coverage verifying that kExecuteJs is
advertised when enabled and omitted when disabled.

zstd: Always build with optimizations, even in debug builds

Since zstd is not something that is debugged, always build it with -O3,
as is done for brotli (which always uses -O2). This makes code that
uses zstd (e.g. decompressing resources or network responses, and
compressing resources at build time) much faster in debug builds.

parent
fabfcf7912fd4ea704e2e37a11cacd6c835833f0 [ diff ] 
[TTC] Show permission-denied toast for denied accounts

When the backend rejects an account after WebSocket upgrade, it closes
the stream cleanly with RFC 6455 code 1008 (`POLICY_VIOLATION`).
Previously, `OnDropChannel` ignored all clean closes, which closed the
TTC popup silently with no toast. In addition, `TtcMesClient` mapped
every model execution error to `kInternalBackendError`, showing a
generic error toast on unsigned profiles.

- Map clean WebSocket 1008 auth or credential closes and HTTP 403
  responses to `ModelExecutionError::kPermissionDenied`.
- Exempt clean 1000 and 1005 closes, map other non-normal closes to
  `ModelExecutionError::kGenericFailure`, and notify observers with
  `DisconnectReason::kError`.
- Add `ttc::ErrorCode::kPermissionDenied`, stop `setup_timer_` on
  streaming errors and disconnects, and skip `OnBackendClosed()` on
  `DisconnectReason::kError` in `TtcMesClient`.
- Report `ErrorCode::kInternalBackendError` if `OnBackendClosed()` runs
  during `kInitializing`, and return early before logging if `kFinished`.
- Register `ToastId::kTtcPermissionDenied` ("Permission denied") with
  metrics variants and unit tests.

[viz] Avoid conflating empty semaphore as succeeding GrContext flush

GrDirectContext flush now differentiates between flush success/failure
from GrSemaphoresSubmitted result and we should check for flush
fSuccess instead of conflating result with whether there were
semaphores passed to flush or not. This change removes such
conditions and just checks for flush fSuccess.

[grid-lanes] Fragmentation - select earlier row breaks

Whole-row fragmentation can break at a boundary with break-before or
break-after avoidance even when an earlier, more appealing boundary is
available.

Track the best preceding row boundary and relayout there when the
current break has lower appeal. Represent row targets as line-type early
breaks, keeping them separate from early breaks inside children.

[Perf] Fix BottomSheetObserver leak in FeedStream

FeedSurfaceActionsHandler.showBottomSheet() registered a new anonymous
BottomSheetObserver on the activity-scoped BottomSheetController every
time the card menu opened and never removed it. Each observer retained
actionSourceView and the enclosing FeedStream until the activity was
destroyed, and every stale observer re-ran on each later sheet close.

Instead of registering an observer, restore focus from
CardMenuBottomSheetContent.destroy(), which the controller calls exactly
once when the content is dismissed or evicted, after which it releases
the content.

[policy] Support AllowDeletingBrowserHistory enterprise policy on iOS

Enterprises need to prevent managed iOS devices from deleting browsing
history. The policy was previously supported on desktop but omitted on
iOS, leaving history deletion unmanaged across iOS UI entry points.

Map AllowDeletingBrowserHistory to the browsing data history deletion
preference via BooleanDisablingPolicyHandler and register the preference
on iOS. Plumb the policy check into IOSBrowsingHistoryDriver,
AutocompleteProviderClientImpl, QuickDeleteMediator, HistoryMediator,
and DownloadListMediator, dynamically disabling deletion actions and
exiting active edit modes on policy updates.

This change was written with AI assistance.

Adds ImageCaptionJob to fetch a saved image, downscale oversized bitmaps
on a background thread, and generate a concise visual caption using the
on-device multimodal Prompt API model when it is already installed on
disk, falling back to an empty caption if the model is unavailable or
the image cannot be fetched.

ContextHubService integration will follow in the next CL.

WebUI Toolbar: set keyboard_navigable on non-Mac.

On Windows and Linux whether toolbar buttons are tab navigable depends
on how the toolbar was last accessed --- access via mouse,
IDC_FOCUS_LOCATION and IDC_FOCUS_SEARCH makes tab and shift-tab skip
over toolbar buttons, while access via IDC_FOCUS_TOOLBAR,
IDC_FOCUS_MENU_BAR, IDC_FOCUS_NEXT_PANE, and IDC_FOCUS_PREVIOUS_PANE
makes them tab focus accessible.

This CL also adjusts the behavior for when the WebUI toolbar is focused
via next/prev pane shortcuts --- that should default to the location
bar, not last focused entry (or first focusable, the way
IDC_FOCUS_TOOLBAR does). That required a bit of help from higher layers
for us to be aware that that's what's happening.

[ozone/wayland] Scale xdg-output bounds given in physical pixels

The xdg-output spec allows a compositor that doesn't scale the monitor
viewport in its compositing space to advertise a logical size equal to
the wl_output mode size (e.g. 3840x2160 for a 3840x2160 mode at scale
2), and the logical position is then in physical pixels as well. Mutter
does this when its logical monitor layout mode is disabled, which is
the default for integer scales without the scale-monitor-framebuffer
experimental feature.

XDGOutput already falls back to wl_output.scale in that case, but the
logical position and size were still used as DIP display bounds, so a
200% display reported 3840x2160 DIP bounds with a device scale factor
of 2. This showed up as screen.width and screen.availWidth being twice
window.outerWidth in web content.

Convert the logical position and size to DIPs with wl_output.scale in
that case, as GTK does. Also treat a logical size equal to the
transposed mode size (90/270 degree transforms, per the spec's example)
the same way, so rotated outputs no longer get a computed scale of 1.

The test server stopped advertising zxdg_output_manager_v1 when aura
output support was retired, so add an opt-in ServerConfig flag for it
and fix a dangling pointer between TestOutput and TestZXdgOutput that
this exposed.

[Linux] Size maximized windows to restore bounds before showing

A popup created with chrome.windows.create({state: "maximized"}) has
no initial bounds, so its X11 window was mapped at 1x1 and only
maximized afterwards. Window managers restore a window to the geometry
it had when it was mapped, so unmaximizing the popup shrank it to 1x1.
SetRestoredBoundsInDIP() only updates Chromium's own copy of the
restore bounds and doesn't help.

DesktopWindowTreeHostPlatform::Show() now sets the window's bounds to
the restore bounds before showing a not-yet-visible window maximized.
Windows that were already created at their restore bounds (e.g.
normal browser windows) are unaffected.

[Android] Optically center the tab switcher button count

TabSwitcherDrawable centered its label on the text bounding box
horizontally and on the font ascent/descent vertically. With Google Sans
this leaves asymmetric glyphs such as "1" roughly 2px right of center at
xxhdpi, and two-digit counts about 1px low.

Horizontally, center on a blend of the ink's center of mass and its
bounding-box center. The center of mass is computed from the glyph
outlines, so nothing is rasterized, and it is cached per label so
repeated draws of the same label do no extra work.

Vertically, center all counts on the digit height and snap the baseline
to a whole pixel, so the baseline does not move from one count to the
next. The overflow labels are centered on their own ink.

Before/after renders and measurement cost:
https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SckR7yV3LWGu6fikzg_Y7yB7LZwGtrXs

Prompt API: Apply responseConstraint in measureContextUsage

LanguageModel::measureContextUsage() ignored options.responseConstraint
and passed an empty schema string to ConvertPromptInputsToMojo(). When
a caller passed a JSON schema with omitResponseConstraintInput left
false, measureContextUsage() omitted the schema text that prompt() and
promptStreaming() append to the user prompt.

Parse and validate options.responseConstraint in measureContextUsage()
with ParseConstraint(), then pass GetSchemaForInput() to
ConvertPromptInputsToMojo().

[OmniboxEverywhere] Drag the window from PreHandleMouseEvent()

Use OmniboxEverywhereWindowDragController (added in the parent CL) to
drag the Loomnibox window on every platform, replacing two
platform-specific paths:
- Aura: OmniboxEverywhereEventHandlerAura, a PreTargetHandler on the
  widget's native window.
- macOS: returning HTCAPTION from the non-client hit test, gated on
  [NSApp currentEvent] (ShouldTreatCurrentEventAsDraggableOnMac()).

This makes Loomnibox the first in-tree consumer of
WebContentsDelegate::PreHandleMouseEvent(). The hook was removed as
unused in crrev.com/c/6880411 (Aug 2025) and re-added in
crrev.com/c/8480402 (Oct 2026) so embedders can handle or drop mouse
events before the renderer sees them. It didn't exist when the split
design was chosen. The original reason for the split ("macOS can't
intercept mouse events / has no pretarget handlers") is only true at
the NSView/Views layer. The content-layer hook runs in the browser
process before the event is forwarded to Blink on every platform, so
no extra renderer round trip is involved. It is wired through the
existing OE-only OmniboxEverywhereContentsWrapper, so no shared
WebUIContentsWrapper code changes.

With the feature enabled, clicks inside draggable regions reach the page
on macOS too. HTCAPTION used to swallow them (and drop :hover).

OmniboxEverywhereUIManager implements the controller's Delegate and
resets it whenever the mouse release may not reach it: deactivation,
Demote(), Close(), widget destruction, and when a modal starts ignoring
input.

Feature: kOmniboxEverywherePreHandleMouseDrag
(chrome://flags#omnibox-everywhere-prehandle-mouse-drag), disabled by
default for now. On macOS the move loop passes the release on to the
page, so a window drag would end with a click where it started; the
follow-up CL holds presses in draggable regions to fix that, and enables
the feature. While it's disabled, the previous Aura pre-target handler
and macOS HTCAPTION paths are unchanged. Both will be removed together
with the flag.

8c46a050bc68ff626cc6ea6fcc3fde7d7de6ccf7 [ diff ] 
[ozone/wayland] Commit non-BMP keysym characters as text

An XKB layout can map a key to a keysym outside the BMP, e.g. U1F642
(🙂). XkbKeyboardLayoutEngine reports it as
DomKey::FromCharacter(0x1F642), but on Wayland nothing consumes the key
when no IME does, so InputMethodAuraLinux inserts it with
TextInputClient::InsertChar(). KeyEvent::GetCharacter() only returns a
char16_t, so the character was truncated to U+F642 (and tripped the
CHECK in GetCharacter()). On X11, GtkIMContextSimple commits such
characters as text instead, which works.

Do the same on Wayland: when the CharacterComposer doesn't filter a key
press whose character is outside the BMP, and no Ctrl/Alt/Meta is held,
WaylandInputMethodContext commits it as UTF-16 text and consumes the
key, so the page sees a "Process" keydown followed by input, as on X11.

Also make KeyEvent::GetCharacter() return 0 for non-BMP characters
instead of a truncated character, since a char16_t can't hold them.
This keeps other paths (e.g. key events with no text input client) from
producing U+F642 or hitting the CHECK. This affects all platforms: e.g.
on ChromeOS, a key with a non-BMP keysym now inserts nothing instead of
a truncated character.

[rust] Fix `rust_dylib` file names and Crubit deps on `dylib`s.

This CL fixes problems of
`override_crate_type_as_dylib_in_component_builds` (which no target
uses yet):

* `tool("rust_dylib")` in the GCC and Apple toolchains used
  `output_prefix = "lib"`, which GN doesn't add if the output name
  already starts with `lib`.  So the `.so` / `.dylib` of a crate like
  `libc` was named `libc_...` instead of `liblibc_...` (which `rustc`
  and `rust_target.gni` expect), and the `.rmeta` of other crates was
  named `liblib...`.  After this CL, both names always start with
  `lib`, like in `tool("rust_rlib")`.
* `cpp_api_from_rust` targets used the internal `..._shared_library`
  target of a `dylib` crate (also for the default header name).  This
  was not allowed by `visibility`, and skipped the `data_deps` of the
  public group (e.g. the copy of the `.so` in the root build
  directory).  After this CL, they use the public target.

This CL also removes an Android-only workaround, because Android no
longer supports component builds.

[tracing] Defer thread pool dependent data sources

The HeapProfilingDataSource and SystemMetricsSampler data sources assume
that the base::ThreadPool is available. This causes crashes if tracing
is enabled before the thread pool is initialized (such as in WebView
with WebViewBackgroundTracingInit enabled).

This CL creates an explicit hook to enable these data sources once it is
safe to do so.

The CL also changes the init order in elevated_tracing_service_delegate
(Windows-specific) to init tracing after the ThreadPool.

[remoting] Bypass VP9 active map when all macroblocks are active

Uses `VideoEncoderActiveMap::SetFull()` on keyframes instead of
rasterizing a full-screen `DesktopRegion`, and skips
`VP8E_SET_ACTIVEMAP` for VP9 (or clears a previously enabled active
map) when all macroblocks are active (`active_blocks() ==
total_blocks()`).

Avoids unnecessary `vpx_codec_control` calls and active-map overhead
on full-screen VP9 delta updates and post-keyframe top-off frames
while preserving partial-frame active-map speedups.

[ios] Stop resetting obscured insets when a navigation commits

CRWWebController reset the web view's obscured insets to zero whenever a
navigation committed, and FullscreenMediator restored them shortly
after. On iOS 26+, where insets are applied as the scroll view's
contentInset, this briefly shifts the page up under the top toolbar,
causing a visible flash on every navigation and reload.

The reset was added in crrev.com/c/7889860 to work around a stale inset
cache in CRWWebViewContentView. Since crrev.com/c/8103676, that cache
check also compares against the scroll view's actual contentInset, and
the bottom-pinned element issue no longer reproduces without the reset.

parent
2558927bb9c480a0eac3ae10c4e8861969ce0eef [ diff ] 
Defer TextFragmentAnchor element fallback to FinalizeAnchor

At the end of layout, Document::ApplyScrollRestorationLogic() calls
LocalFrameView::InvokeFragmentAnchor() to scroll to any pending URL
fragment. When a text fragment directive fails to match,
TextFragmentAnchor::DidFinishSearch() previously called
ElementFragmentAnchor::TryCreate() synchronously to fall back to the
element fragment.

However, ElementFragmentAnchor::TryCreate() has side effects that can
run script and mutate the DOM: it updates the CSS :target element,
unlocks content-visibility: auto ancestors, and calls
DisplayLockUtilities::RevealAutoExpandableAncestors() to synchronously
dispatch beforematch and reveal hidden="until-found" and <details>
ancestors. Running this at the end of layout executes script and mutates
the DOM mid-lifecycle, dirtying style and layout right after the
document reaches kLayoutClean (regressing DocumentLifecycle to
kVisualUpdatePending and triggering a DCHECK in FrameCaret).

Furthermore, TextFragmentAnchor::FinalizeAnchor() runs in a pre-rAF
animation frame task before the frame's style and layout pass, but
previously called ElementFragmentAnchor::Installed() and Invoke()
immediately. Because Invoke() scrolls the target into view using
existing layout geometry without forcing layout, any target revealed or
dirtied by TryCreate() and beforematch had not been laid out yet and
failed to scroll into view.

To fix this:
- Defer ElementFragmentAnchor::TryCreate() from DidFinishSearch() to
  FinalizeAnchor(), where script execution and DOM mutations are safe.
- Install the fallback ElementFragmentAnchor on LocalFrameView via
  SetFragmentAnchor(), which calls Installed() immediately and leaves
  Invoke() to run after style and layout update later in the same frame.

[SendTabToSelf] Remove redundant SetHighlightedElement call

This CL removes the SetHighlightedElement() call in
SendTabToSelfBubbleController::ShowBubbleWithAnchor(). The bubble is
already constructed with the toolbar button (or overflow button) anchor,
which BubbleDialogDelegate highlights automatically on display. Removing
the explicit element-identifier lookup avoids crashes when multiple
elements temporarily share the same identifier during toolbar fade-out
animations and fixes highlighting when the button is overflowed.

[WebUIToolbar] Remove keep_anchor_visible from profile menu APIs

Pressing the avatar button wrapped the press in RunWhenVisible() only to
get a token that kept the button visible, and passed it through the
button actions to ProfileMenuCoordinator::Show(). This token is
redundant, because the coordinator calls RunWhenVisible() again before
showing the bubble and holds its own token until the bubble closes.

Handle presses directly and drop the token from Show(), the button
actions and HandleButtonPressed(). Explicit button actions now run right
away instead of waiting for an overflowed WebUI avatar button to be
shown. An overflowed avatar button now pops out after the async promo
lookup finishes, rather than immediately on press.

a75bfe5fdd1ed27d2959d2e2d819c5264cb4bc98 [ diff ] 
[WebAuthn] Ignore passwords for cross-origin Ambient and Immediate

An Ambient or Immediate mode WebAuthn request from a cross-origin
iframe, if it contains both `publicKey` and `password` requests, will
hang the request until cancelled, effectively making it a no-op.

Passwords are not supported from cross-origin iframes, but since
passkeys can be provided when the appropriate feature policy is
present, this change allows the request to proceed but passwords will
be ignored.

This also addresses an issue with same-origin iframes, which was a
problem with using `IsPrimaryMainFrame` in
`ChromeAuthenticatorRequestDelegate`. Now there is an explicit
check in `AuthenticatorCommonImpl`.

[ArcAutoLaunch] Relax AutoLaunchAndroidApps policy description

The AutoLaunchAndroidApps description stated that the listed apps must
also be force-installed through ArcPolicy, but ArcAutoLaunchService does
not check this, and an app explicitly listed by the admin should be
launched regardless of how it was installed. Update the description to
reflect the actual behavior and note that admins can only configure the
setting for force-installed apps.

scrollbar and keyboard variants, so a problem with one input type no

test's now-unused TestExpectations entry.

f9ae3078d6e0b2fcd3ad08a5a65a3f2dae585b59
parent
9143e42b5ec2eba8986b46d56aa104136fc6f5f4 [ diff ] 
blink: Cancel pending P2PAsyncAddressResolver on resolver destruction

AsyncDnsAddressResolverImpl starts P2PAsyncAddressResolver, which
transitions into kStateSent and binds a scoped_refptr to itself into the
GetHostAddress Mojo callback. Unlike the legacy AsyncAddressResolverImpl
it replaced, ~AsyncDnsAddressResolverImpl() did not call Cancel(), so
destroying an in-flight resolver left P2PAsyncAddressResolver in
kStateSent and tripped the ~P2PAsyncAddressResolver() DCHECK when Mojo
dropped the callback during shared headless_shell tab teardown.

Call resolver_->Cancel() in ~AsyncDnsAddressResolverImpl() to mark the
request finished on teardown.

This eliminates the shared-tab WebRTC resolver cleanup crashes affecting
subsequent WPTs on mac-rel.

FSA: Enforce named bucket quota for sync access handle writes

FileSystemAccessFileModificationHostImpl checked capacity requests
against the StorageKey's usage and quota only, so writes through
FileSystemSyncAccessHandle could exceed a named Storage Bucket's quota
while the same write through createWritable() was rejected. Use
QuotaManagerProxy::GetBucketSpaceRemaining(), which checks both the
bucket and the StorageKey, matching SandboxFileStreamWriter.

GetBucketSpaceRemaining() is made virtual on QuotaManagerProxy and
QuotaManagerImpl so test doubles can override it, like
GetUsageAndQuota(). MockQuotaManager now implements it using its own
buckets, quotas and usage.

explicit profile-scoped and global APIs to support multi-profile on

[WebUI toolbar] Make toolbar's WebView span full toolbar height

With the WebUI toolbar, the avatar and app menu chips switch to an
outset focus ring (2px outline, 2px offset) when they show a label. The
ring's top and bottom were clipped.

* CSS already centers the controls vertically, and native siblings are
  centered by the FlexLayout cross-axis alignment, so nothing moves.
* The toolbar's height caps now add the default vertical margin instead
  of the layout's current one, so the toolbar height is unchanged.
* The WebUI back button no longer stretches to the full row height, so
  its click target still matches the native button.
* The strips above and below the controls are draggable in vertical tabs
  mode through the existing draggable region.

With the room this leaves, the location bar's focus ring no longer has
to be inset to avoid clipping, so draw it 1px outside and 1px inside the
location bar, like native. This makes 1px more room inside location bar.

Toolbar buttons, such as the extension buttons, intentionally keep their
focus ring fully inside the button (the WebUI inset box-shadow ring, as
in cr-icon-button). Native draws it 1px outside and 1px inside the
button. Keeping the WebUI ring looks cleaner, especially next to the
extensions container border. We can change them in the future if we
decide to.

fuzzilli: Drop --jit-fuzzing in Fuzzilli builds of js_in_process_fuzzer

Fuzzilli builds of js_in_process_fuzzer fuzz the browser's Mojo interfaces,
not V8. --jit-fuzzing makes V8 optimize functions after a handful of calls,
on background threads, which adds coverage that does not depend on the
program and makes executions slower. Leave it out of Fuzzilli builds.

[remoting] Apply initial rate-control params before VPX encoder init

Passes `FrameParams` into `WebrtcVideoEncoderVpx::Configure()` so
initial `rc_target_bitrate`, `rc_min_quantizer`, and
`rc_max_quantizer` are set on `config_` before `vpx_codec_enc_init()`,
instead of initializing at the 100 kbps floor and immediately calling
`vpx_codec_enc_config_set()` in `UpdateConfig()`.

Eliminates a redundant `vpx_codec_enc_config_set()` on initial encode
and resize, prevents post-keyframe QP clamping (+3.0 to +5.5 dB min
PSNR on scrolling/window motion), and fixes 40%-44% bitrate undershoot
on portrait VP9 workloads.

52cc9cb2e8d5cae618cdb15a6e9c41e002f2ddf2 [ diff ] 
Do not cancel already-finished CSS transitions and animations

When a `display` allow-discrete transition (such as closing a
`<dialog>` with `::backdrop`) or a non-filling CSS animation keeping
a `display: none` element visible reaches its end time before
`BeginMainFrame` — or during style recalc on the frame it finishes —
`CSSAnimations::Cancel()` cancels the animation instead of letting it
finish. This rejects `.finished` promises with `AbortError`, fires
spurious `cancel`/`transitioncancel` events, and transitions
`playState` to `idle`.

Avoid canceling animations whose computed play state is already
`finished` (for CSS animations, only when the effect is no longer in
effect so `forwards`-filling animations are still canceled on
`display: none`), treat `finished` transitions as finished rather than
canceled when retargeted or removed from `transition-property`, and
schedule a frame service if the animation is still active so its
finish notification and end events are dispatched. Also cache the
originating `EventTarget` on `AnimationEventDelegate` and
`TransitionEventDelegate` so events on disposed pseudo-elements
(e.g. `::backdrop`) still target the originating element on the next
frame.

[glic] Move mode and GetContext error metrics to GlicInstanceMetrics

Move web client mode tracking (web_client_mode_) and the
Glic.Api.GetContext*.Error and Glic.Api.GetImageBytesFromTab.Error
histograms from profile-scoped GlicMetrics to GlicInstanceMetrics so
concurrent instances with different modes do not overwrite each other.

Record these histograms through GlicMetricReporter so they are also
emitted per provider (Glic.Consumer.* / Glic.Enterprise.*).
